concerns.concern: Joule heating (~6–8 mW in the device region) could cause sample drift, Bragg-peak shifts and M1/R fraction changes. Any of these would decorrelate the speckle without domain rearrangement. No peak-centroid tracking, drift correction or heating-only control is reported to exclude this.
concerns.quote: Joule heating, thermal drift and lattice-parameter changes are not excluded as the cause of speckle decorrelation.

concerns.concern: The rising cycle-to-cycle correlation interpreted as 'learning' could instead reflect thermal/mechanical settling of the setup, or incomplete Off-state relaxation. Controls such as Off-state imaging, varied Off time, no-current runs, a reference reflection and the full lag matrix are missing.
concerns.quote: The rising cycle-to-cycle correlation ("learning", Fig. 3c,i) has trivial alternative explanations that are not ruled out.

concerns.concern: The claims of deterministic switching and recovered stochasticity are not backed by any cycle-resolved electrical statistics (threshold distributions, delay jitter, resistance versus cycle). XPCS of the On state is only a proxy, and the 1 s exposure does not probe the nucleation event.
concerns.quote: "Deterministic switching" and "recovered stochasticity" are never measured electrically.

concerns.concern: Fitted relaxation times are 5–50 times longer than the measurement windows, so g₂ decays by only ~0.2–0.5%. In this regime τ, β, contrast and baseline are strongly covariant, and the quoted uncertainties are implausibly small. It is also unstated whether contrast and baseline are fixed or free.
concerns.quote: The fitted τ values are 5–50× longer than the ~3,000–10,000 s windows over which each g₂ is measured

concerns.concern: The text and Fig. 2c disagree on the room-temperature stability limit (8000 s vs 81,000 s). If the lower value is correct, most driven-state τ values exceed the instrumental stability floor and cannot be distinguished from drift.
concerns.quote: The text also gives the room-temperature stability limit as "8000 ± 3000 s", whereas Fig. 2c reports 81,000 ± 3,000 s.

concerns.concern: The apparent rise of β from ~1 to ~1.5 may be a fitting artefact: a single τ is imposed while β varies, so genuine aging of τ could be absorbed into β. The β points also have large error bars and scatter, and no χ², residuals or covariance are given.
concerns.quote: The β ≈ 1 → 1.5 "transition" may be an artefact of the fitting constraint.

concerns.concern: A compressed exponent has many generic origins in XPCS (drift, heating, heterodyne mixing, aging). None of the hallmarks of jamming are shown: q-dependence of τ, dynamic heterogeneity, a control parameter, divergence. Mechanistic statements about domains lack real-space or phase-fraction support.
concerns.quote: The "jamming transition" interpretation is not supported by independent evidence.

concerns.concern: A sub-threshold current with no percolating filament shows the same β evolution as the switching current. This contradicts the claim that switching induces jamming. The switching state of each current (e.g. 1.7 mA) and the simultaneous resistance traces are not shown.
concerns.quote: Sub-threshold, non-switching currents show the same β evolution, which undermines the link between jamming and switching.

concerns.concern: The causal link between jamming and learning rests only on coincident ~10³ s timescales from different protocols (constant current vs on/off cycling). These timescales also coincide with setup thermalization. β and τ should be analysed within the cycling data, or the causal claim removed from the title.
concerns.quote: The causal link between "jamming" and "learning" asserted in the title is inferred only from coincident timescales.

concerns.concern: The claimed sequence of training, erasure by sub-threshold current and retraining is never demonstrated. Erasure was measured only on an untrained state, and retention after training was not tested.
concerns.quote: The train/erase/retrain functionality claimed in the abstract is never demonstrated.

concerns.concern: ΔG is min–max normalized to [0,1] without a definition, so a value of 1 does not mean identical configurations. The absolute change in G between the stochastic and deterministic regimes appears small.
concerns.quote: ΔG(n,n+1) is normalized min–max to [0,1] without the normalization being defined.

concerns.concern: The high cumulative X-ray dose on the thin VO₂ film could itself cause oxygen vacancies, heating or metallization, and so drive decorrelation or stabilization. No dose-rate, attenuated-beam, beam on/off or fresh-spot controls are shown.
concerns.quote: Possible X-ray beam-induced effects are not addressed.

concerns.concern: The Joule-heating/Arrhenius interpretation is internally inconsistent. The 4 mA On-state τ is slower than the room-temperature no-current τ, even though the device should be hotter. The local temperature under bias is never estimated.
concerns.quote: the 4 mA On-state τ (~1.5–1.6×10⁵ s) is slower than the 298 K no-current τ (8.1×10⁴ s), even though the device should be hotter.

concerns.concern: The correlation function is normalized by the whole-acquisition ⟨I²⟩ rather than the standard pixel-averaged intensities. Any change in total diffracted intensity therefore appears as decorrelation. The ROI, averaging and determination of the contrast A are also unspecified.
concerns.quote: The correlation-function definitions and normalization are non-standard and under-specified.

concerns.concern: The beam is larger than the device channel and illuminates static regions and electrodes, causing heterodyne-like mixing that biases τ and β. The coherence length is much smaller than the illuminated area. It is unclear what fraction of the signal the filament contributes.
concerns.quote: The beam footprint and coherence geometry leave it unclear what the speckle actually reports.

concerns.concern: It is unclear whether the closely spaced M1 and R reflections are resolved, which one is tracked, and how their contributions are separated. The speckle changes could arise from twin, variant, M2/T or strain domains rather than metal/insulator domains.
concerns.quote: The phase selectivity and the attribution to metallic/insulating domains are not demonstrated.

concerns.concern: Ga-irradiation defects could act as pinning sites that guide filament location and by themselves explain deterministic switching; this is not discussed. The pristine-device results supporting generality appear only in the SI without quantitative comparison.
concerns.quote: Ga-induced defects could act as pinning sites that guide filament location and could themselves explain deterministic switching, yet this is not discussed.

concerns.concern: Each key result appears to come from a single run on a single device. No run-to-run or device-to-device reproducibility is shown, and the dependence on current amplitude and duty cycle is not explored.
concerns.quote: Statistics and reproducibility are minimal.

concerns.concern: The activation energy is derived from only two or three temperatures. One of them (340 K) lies in the non-stationary hysteretic transition, so the value is not robust.
concerns.quote: E_a = 230 ± 70 meV from so few points in a non-equilibrium regime is not robust.

concerns.concern: Comparing E_a/k_B to the melting point conflates a domain-wall barrier height with a thermodynamic transition temperature and has no clear physical basis.
concerns.quote: conflates a barrier height for domain-wall motion with a thermodynamic transition temperature. It has no clear physical basis.

concerns.concern: The claimed trend that larger currents give slower jamming rests on t_jam values that are statistically indistinguishable. At 4 mA the sigmoid does not clearly plateau within the window.
concerns.quote: These values are statistically indistinguishable.

concerns.concern: The shear-thickening analogy is physically inapt, since shear thickening concerns viscosity rising with drive rate rather than a delay to a jammed state. Calling the result a 'transition' overstates the data.
concerns.quote: shear thickening concerns viscosity increasing with drive rate, not a delay to a jammed state, so the analogy is physically inapt.

concerns.concern: The irradiation geometry is described inconsistently (central 5×5 µm region vs globally irradiated), and the dose units given in different places need reconciling.
concerns.quote: The main text says a central 5×5 µm region was irradiated with 0.1 pC/µm², whereas Methods say devices were "globally irradiated".

concerns.concern: The domain-size estimate from the peak width may be dominated by film thickness, strain, mosaicity or instrumental resolution. The direction of the momentum-transfer width is not stated.
concerns.quote: R_d = 2π/Q_FWHM = 20 ± 4 nm may be dominated by finite film thickness (45 nm), strain inhomogeneity, mosaicity or instrumental resolution

concerns.concern: There are several numerical and figure inconsistencies: 0.26 vs 0.27 mA, 150,000 vs 160,000 s, a nonexistent inset in Fig. 3i, t_age definition, Fig. 1 panel labels, and cycle timing not matching ~1800 cycles in ~5000 s.
concerns.quote: Several numerical, textual and figure inconsistencies should be corrected.

concerns.concern: The terminology is inaccurate. The compressed exponent is called a 'stretching' exponent, 'single exponential' is used for a stretched/compressed form, and calling VO₂ a 'Mott insulator' needs qualification.
concerns.quote: "Single exponential" is used for a stretched/compressed form.

concerns.concern: The ~10³ s memory, erasure and jamming timescales are far from practical neuromorphic operating speeds, and this gap is not discussed.
concerns.quote: The authors should discuss the gap between these timescales and practical neuromorphic operating speeds.

concerns.concern: The novelty is not clearly separated from established prior work on ramp-reversal memory, persistent metallic domains, scarring, subthreshold firing and glassy XPCS dynamics in oxides.
concerns.quote: The novelty should be delineated more carefully against prior work.
